items.stem: The NSSO primarily uses:
items.explanation: The NSSO, now part of the National Statistical Office, conducts large-scale socio-economic surveys using stratified multi-stage sampling so that geographically dispersed populations can be surveyed efficiently.

items.stem: The National Statistical Commission was set up on the recommendation of:
items.explanation: The National Statistical Commission followed the recommendations of the Rangarajan Commission, which proposed reforms to the Indian statistical system.

items.stem: The NSO was formed by merging:
items.explanation: The National Statistical Office was created in 2019 by merging the Central Statistics Office and the National Sample Survey Office.

items.stem: Stratified sampling is most efficient when strata are:
items.explanation: Stratification is most effective when units within each stratum are similar. Homogeneous strata reduce within-stratum sampling variance.

items.stem: Cluster sampling is most efficient when clusters are:
items.explanation: Cluster sampling is most efficient when each cluster is internally heterogeneous and resembles a small version of the population; this makes selected clusters representative.

items.stem: Multi-stage sampling is used mainly because:
options: no complete frame of ultimate units exists
it is more precise than SRS
items.explanation: Multi-stage sampling is practical when a complete list of ultimate sampling units is unavailable. Frames can instead be prepared successively for larger and then smaller sampling units.

items.stem: P. C. Mahalanobis is associated with:
options: a distance measure in multivariate analysis
items.explanation: P. C. Mahalanobis founded the Indian Statistical Institute and is associated with the Mahalanobis distance, a covariance-adjusted measure of multivariate distance.

items.stem: The first-stage units in NSSO rural surveys are:
items.explanation: In rural survey designs, census villages are commonly used as first-stage sampling units; households or individuals are selected at later stages.

items.stem: Double sampling is used when:
options: auxiliary information must be collected on a large preliminary sample
items.explanation: Double sampling first collects auxiliary information from a large preliminary sample, then obtains the more expensive study variable from a subsample.

items.stem: MoSPI was formed in:
items.explanation: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation was formed in 1999 by bringing together the Department of Statistics and the Department of Programme Implementation.

items.stem: The National Statistical Commission was constituted in:
items.explanation: The National Statistical Commission was constituted in 2005, following the recommendations of the 2001 Rangarajan Commission report.

items.stem: The Kothari Commission dealt with:
items.explanation: The Kothari Commission (1964–66) was the Indian Education Commission; it examined the structure and development of education.

items.stem: The Indian Statistical Institute was founded by:
items.explanation: The Indian Statistical Institute was founded in 1931 by P. C. Mahalanobis in Kolkata.

items.stem: The Central Statistics Office was established in:
items.explanation: The Central Statistical Organisation was established in 1951 to coordinate statistical activities and develop national statistical standards.

items.stem: The National Statistical Office was created by merging:
items.explanation: The National Statistical Office was formed by merging the Central Statistics Office and the National Sample Survey Office.

items.stem: The Census of India is conducted by:
items.explanation: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India is responsible for conducting the Census of India.

items.stem: The Kelkar Committee is associated with:
items.explanation: The Kelkar Committee is associated with tax reforms, including recommendations on direct and indirect taxation.

items.stem: The National Family Health Survey is conducted under the aegis of:
items.explanation: The National Family Health Survey is conducted under the aegis of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with IIPS serving as the nodal agency.

items.stem: The Index of Industrial Production is compiled by:
items.explanation: The Index of Industrial Production is compiled by the national statistical office, historically the CSO and now within the NSO framework.

items.stem: The Chief Statistician of India serves as:
items.explanation: The Chief Statistician of India serves as Secretary to the National Statistical Commission, supporting its administrative and statistical coordination.
